design: RMIT (randomized multiple interleaved trials): fresh random permutation of (strategy, concurrency) pairs per repetition; server restarted before every run.

machine_specs.processor: unrecorded (script bug at run time hardcoded the i3 laptop's processor string here; actual hardware was an Azure Standard_D4s_v6 VM, 4 vCPU / 16GB RAM, Central India region — fixed in benchmarks/run_rmit_experiment.py's collect_machine_specs to detect real hardware going forward)

notes: Run on a dedicated Azure Standard_D4s_v6 VM (4 vCPU / 16GB RAM, Central India), provisioned solely for this run and deleted immediately afterward. Nothing else was running on the VM — no agent session, no GUI, no other processes — so this is the 'clean' run the earlier laptop dataset (experiment_results_rmit/) could not be, since that one ran alongside an active Claude Code session.

temp_max_celsius and battery/AC fields are null throughout: this is a VM with no thermal sensors or battery, and benchmarks/system_state.py degrades to None for unavailable sysfs paths rather than failing, as designed.

Result: no configuration was flagged as bimodal (0/48), and relative 95% CI width was <=0.0175 for every configuration (tighter than the laptop run's <=0.039), with paired throughput ratios vs the disabled baseline all within 0.977-1.005 — i.e. instrumentation overhead was small and within noise once the machine was genuinely idle and randomized ordering was used.
